title: Interacting quantum reference frames
authors: Leonardo Chataignier, Alexander R. H. Smith
abstract: We formulate quantum reference frames within the Dirac quantization of gauge theories, where physical states are obtained from a kinematical Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_{\rm kin}$ by group averaging. We assume the gauge group $G$ is unimodular, and we define a quantum reference frame as a system of coherent states associated with a group $G_R$ of frame orientations acting on a tensor factor of $\mathcal{H}_{\rm kin}$. In direct analogy with the Faddeev-Popov procedure in path integrals, we show that the physical inner product can be written in terms of a choice of frame orientation with an appropriate operator measure, but that the physical Hilbert space is independent of this choice of frame. This yields a generalization of the Page-Wootters reduction map used to define conditional states and conditional probabilities of measurement outcomes given a frame orientation. These probabilities correspond to the expectation values of relational Dirac observables obtained from generalizations of previously considered relativization maps. Our main result is that the map that implements a change of frame is unitary, even when $G$ does not act as a tensor-product representation across a factorization of $\mathcal{H}_{\rm kin}$. The formalism therefore accommodates interactions between reference frames and the systems described relative to them. We apply this formalism to temporal frames, showing that a unitary Schrödinger equation emerges for an interacting clock and system, and that a previously reported time-nonlocal Schrödinger equation is recovered in an appropriate limit. With this, problems of non-unitarity are avoided by the use of the gauge-fixing measure in the physical inner product. We also discuss the case of interacting spatial frames, where the known correspondence between coherence in one frame and entanglement in another is shown to depend on the coupling.
summary: This work develops a formalism for quantum reference frames in gauge theories, extending previous work to include interactions between the reference frame and the system. By proving the unitarity of the change-of-frame map, the authors provide a consistent, gauge-invariant description that avoids non-unitarity issues common in such setups. This is crucial for applying quantum mechanics to scenarios involving relative motion or time measurement.
main_problem: The paper addresses the formulation of quantum reference frames within the Dirac quantization of gauge theories, specifically tackling the challenge of interactions between the reference frame and the system while maintaining unitarity.
main_result: The change-of-frame map is proven to be unitary, even when the gauge group does not act as a simple tensor product, allowing for a consistent description of interacting reference frames.
method: The authors use group averaging techniques analogous to the Faddeev-Popov procedure to define the physical inner product and generalize the Page-Wootters reduction map to handle conditional states.
model_or_system: The system involves a kinematical Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_{\rm kin}$ factorized into a reference frame sector ($H_R$) and a system sector ($H_S$), governed by a locally compact, unimodular gauge group $G$.
key_observables: Relational Dirac observables and the physical inner product, which is shown to be independent of the chosen frame orientation.
important_parameters: The gauge group $G$ must be unimodular; the formalism successfully yields a unitary Schrödinger equation for interacting temporal frames.
main_assumptions: The gauge group $G$ is assumed to be locally compact and unimodular. The formalism builds upon the structure of gauge theories and the concept of group averaging.
paper_structure: The paper develops the formalism by first establishing the gauge-invariant physical Hilbert space via group averaging, then introducing the frame-dependent structure using coherent states, and finally proving the unitarity of the change-of-frame map to accommodate interactions.
why_interesting: The core result on the unitarity of the change-of-frame map is highly relevant for any field dealing with relational observables or time evolution in curved/non-inertial backgrounds, as it provides a rigorous framework for treating interactions.
